searchText: We have seen quite some releases from each client team even in the last week. Some are criticial, some aren't. Is there a reason client teams decide to push out an update so close to the mainnet fork date? I'd just prefer if client teams would be a bit more cautious regarding last minute releases, as they might introduce unexpected regression, that couldn't have been tested so close to the fork date. I understand that some bumps are minor, but its still a bit worrisome - from the testing point of view. I'd much prefer to have these small fixes rolled out potentially once the fork transition is completed, that way we can be sure that the code tested with shadowforks and previous devnets is the code that will be rolled out on mainnet. I think it's a consequence of shorter hardforks. I don't know how other teams are feeling, but we kept improving the codebase after the official mainnet release for Fusaka. I guess what is happening is an acceptable situation given tight schedules. Imo only critical releases should be pushed between the date of announcement of releases and mainnet fork date. it's when the fix was available, and I think you yourself seemed to view the underlying issue as fairly important I agree though, in general I think client releases should not be blocked by the fork in general, we do not expect all users to upgrade unless we explicitly announce otherwise so it is fine to release at any time only issue is that the new release might hide some nasty regression that we might or might not be able to catch before we hit mainnet such regressions are generally not a big deal once the fork has gone through, but it can be pretty bad just a few days before the fork but this can always happen regressions in block processing are always a big deal it's not tied to the fork we could, theoretically, mess up any fork code path at any time but in practice it doesn't happen very often because we have lots of testing in place and review procedures so these same procedures also protect us around the time of the fork I'm just answering like this because I want to take the fear out of releasing. it's important to always be able to release a new client version > We have seen quite some releases from each client team even in the last week. Some are criticial, some aren't. Is there a reason client teams decide to push out an update so close to the mainnet fork date? Perhaps we should be more careful and wait for a few months without bugs on testnets before setting a mainnet release date? the contention between Barnabas pushing to ship faster and Barnabas pushing to not update with bug fixes is not solvable. Claude is not that good yet I'm not saying that we shouldn't have releases post the announcement, but shipping unrelated features seems risky.
